COP.thesis_one_line: Low-cost oil and gas giant returning about 45% of operating cash to shareholders, but the share price already assumes oil stays elevated for years.
kill_criteria: Consolidated total debt to capital (10-Q "Financial Indicators" table) above 35% (now 26%).
FY2026 production guidance midpoint cut below 2.295 MMBOED (the current low end) at any release.
Total 2026 capital raised above $12.5B (the top of the "$12 to $12.5 billion" range, acc. 0001163165-26-000016) without a matching production raise.
Shareholder distributions below 40% of CFO for two consecutive quarters (stated target 45%).
Reported production down more than 4% y/y on a deal-adjusted basis for two more consecutive quarters (Q2'26: -4%).
key_adverse_facts: Full-year 2026 production guidance cut at the Q1 release from 2.33-2.36 to 2.295-2.325 MMBOED (Qatar excluded, Surmont royalty) and capex range raised to $12-12.5B from ~$12B; Q2 release maintained both.
Q2'26 production 2,248 MBOED vs 2,391 a year earlier (-6% reported, -4% deal-adjusted); earnings growth is price-driven (Brent $104.52 vs $67.82).
Consolidated total debt $23.3B vs cash and short-term investments $7.7B; 2025 reserve replacement 80% (organic 99%) per 10-K.
New Iraq (Kirkuk 42% JV) and Syria exposure plus Qatar LNG disruption.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q04) gave no red flags and cited general knowledge; filings show a guidance cut and a Middle East production disruption in 2026.
V1 TTM capex $10.16B vs company 'Capital expenditures and investments' TTM ~$11.9B, so V1 TTM FCF $11.8B vs ~$10.0B here.
V1 base 3y -24.4%/yr relies on consensus FY1 EPS -6.7% and de-rating to 10.1x; futures strip and company plan support roughly +5.6%/yr base.
COP.next_earnings_date_basis: estimated from 6 Nov 2025 pattern; not announced in filings read
COP.confidence_in_thesis: medium (primary filings read for 4 releases, 10-Q and 10-K; outcome depends on the oil deck, an assumption anchored on the futures strip)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Both say not cheap. V1 base -24%/yr leans on falling consensus EPS and de-rating to the 10.1x peer median; my strip-based base is +5.6%/yr, below an ~8.5% hurdle. Reverse DCF implies ~2.0% 10-year FCF growth vs my ~3% base (in line, no margin of safety).

COP.scenario_basis: Start $127.30, TTM adjusted EPS $7.76 (FY25 $6.16); 2029E EPS base ~$11.6 at Brent ~$75 strip (bear ~$7.8 at $58, bull ~$16.2 at $95) incl. ~4.6%/yr net buyback shrink and half of the stated $7B FCF inflection; exit P/E 12x base/10x bear/12x bull; dividends ~$10.6 over 3 years ($0.84/qtr growing ~4%).

APA.thesis_one_line: Oil producer with Permian, Egypt and Suriname assets; cheap if oil tracks the futures curve, but exposed to a price slump.
kill_criteria: Consolidated net debt (8-K "Reconciliation of debt to net debt") above $4.5B (now $3.3B).
Adjusted production below 330,000 BOE/d in any quarter (Q2'26: 347,000).
U.S. oil production guidance cut below 120,000 b/d (now 123,000).
Company-defined quarterly free cash flow negative in any quarter with WTI above $70.
GranMorgu first-oil date guided later than 2029 (10-K FY25: "First oil is anticipated in 2028").
key_adverse_facts: Adjusted production is shrinking: 392k BOE/d FY25, guided 371k for 2026, 347k in Q2'26.

Q2'26 realised U.S. gas price was $(2.98)/Mcf (8-K Ex-99.1 2026-08-05; earlier text said ($2.20)); 10-Q: gas production -142.0 MMcf/d and NGL -7.5 Mb/d YoY, primarily from Alpine High/Permian curtailments on weak Waha prices.

Q2'26 earnings include a large third-party purchased oil and gas margin ($345M pre-tax net gain incl. $109M hedge loss, 8-K 8 Jul 2026); Q2'25 GAAP EPS $1.67 included a $282M divestiture gain (adjusted $0.87).

Egypt PSC tax barrels mute price upside; Sinopec owns one-third NCI (H1'26 NCI income $177M, distributions $164M); Quadrant/Santos (~AUD 57M counterclaims plus ~AUD 133M tax claim) and Delaware climate suits pending.
data_conflicts: V1 flags D3 TTM revenue $2.43B vs Yahoo $8.57B and missing capex (proxied by D&A): V1 TTM FCF $4.5B / 14% yield is overstated; company-defined TTM FCF is ~$1.96B (13% of market cap).
Triage (Q04) cited an 84% 12-month rally and negative forward EPS; filings show raised guidance items in each of the last four releases but falling adjusted production.

APA.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-medium (primary filings read; normalised FCF depends on the deck assumption and an FCF sensitivity derived from H1'26 vs 2025)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Verdict agrees (fair, not a clear include). V1 base -5.6%/yr and FCF yield rely on broken D3 revenue/capex inputs and falling consensus EPS; using company-defined FCF and the futures strip my base is about +6%/yr. Reverse DCF implies about -1.9% FCF growth vs ~0% base (below, as originally computed), but the return does not clear a ~10% hurdle given the -17% bear. [DV04 2026-10-06 restatement: cost of equity 10% was not tied to the 5.17% 10-yr UST plus ERP and SBC (~$107M) was not deducted; at Ke 11.2% (beta 1.2, ERP 5%) on FCF $1.593B the implied 10-year growth is about +0.8% (range -0.9% to +2.8%) vs ~0% base, so implied_vs_base is in_line; WATCH unchanged.]

ROST.thesis_one_line: Leading off-price clothing chain, growing fast with net cash, but priced near 30 times underlying earnings after a one-off tariff-refund windfall.
kill_criteria: Comparable-store sales below +2% in two consecutive quarters (guidance: "Comparable store sales are now expected to increase 6% to 7% in the third quarter and 4% to 5% in the fourth quarter.", acc. 0000745732-26-000038).
Quarterly operating margin ex one-offs below 11.5% (Q2'26 ex-refund 13.5%).
FY26 EPS guide cut below $8.01 (low end of "$8.61 to $8.77" less the $0.60 refund).
Consolidated inventory growth exceeds sales growth by more than 10 points (now +18% vs +13%).
Consolidated cash and equivalents minus consolidated debt (current plus long-term) falls below $2.0B (now $3.27B; debt $1.02B).
key_adverse_facts: Q2'26 EPS $2.66 includes ~$0.60 (about $253M pre-tax) of one-off IEEPA tariff refunds; FY26 guide $8.61-$8.77 includes it, so ex-refund is ~$8.01-$8.17.
H1'26 operating margin (13.4% in Q1, 13.5% ex-refund in Q2) is a record-level base; H2 comps guided to +6-7% and +4-5% on tougher comparisons after +17% and +10%.
Inventory $3.09B vs $2.61B a year earlier (+18%) against Q2 sales +13%.
Price ~27x FY26 guide midpoint and ~29x ex-refund.
data_conflicts: V1 implied 10-year growth 17.8% is a fading year-1 rate on FCFF with SBC not added back; my constant-CAGR equivalent is 9.7-10.7% after the DV36 2026-10-09 restatement (was 8.4-9.3%); both say the price needs bull-case delivery.
V1 consensus FY0 EPS $8.63 includes the refund; normalise before using it as a run-rate.
